events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWAKQ

The National Weather Service in Wakefield has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Gloucester County in southeastern Virginia...
York County in southeastern Virginia...

* Until 345 PM EDT.

* At 1243 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Gloucester Point, Virginia Institute For Marine Sciences, Seaford,
Queens Lake, Wicomico, Achilles, Carver Gardens, York Terrace,
Yorktown, Ordinary, Lackey, U.s. Naval Weapons, White Marsh, Glass,
Harris Grove, Hornsbyville and Naxera.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Southwest San Juan Mountains; San Juan River Basin
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, San Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The ground remains saturated from recent heavy rainfall over the
past week. After a brief break, deep moisture is expected to
return to southwest Colorado Tuesday with a few inches of
rainfall possible during the Wednesday through Thursday
timeframe. In addition, multiple rounds of showers and
thunderstorms are expected Wednesday through Thursday evening
producing periods of heavy rainfall and potential flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
